sentences.text: Amanzia is a genus of turiasaurian sauropod dinosaur, a group of large herbivores, found in the Late Jurassic Reuchenette Formation in Moutier, Switzerland.
The fossil bones are not articulated, are strongly compressed, and were often damaged during removal from the rock.
Amanzia is the first sauropod dinosaur to be named from remains found in Switzerland.
In 2007, the rare preservation of fossilized cartilage in a limb joint was reported.

The species was originally classified under the names Megalosaurus meriani, Cetiosauriscus greppini, and Ornithopsis greppini before being moved to the genus Amanzia. After cleaning and preparation in 2003, it was realized that the fossils were not closely related to Cetiosauriscus. The genus name Amanzia was established in 2020 by Schwarz et al. in honor of Amanz Gressly, the first person to discover dinosaur bones in Switzerland.

While von Huene originally thought the material represented two or three individuals, a 2020 study concluded there were at least four individuals. Among the four individuals, two are similar in size, one is 15% longer, and one is 20% shorter.
In 2020, seventy-five additional sauropod specimens from the same site were referred to the species Amanzia greppini.
The fossils date to the Kimmeridgian stage, between 152.7 and 152 million years ago.
The dinosaur lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately 155 million years ago, in what is now Europe. The time range for Amanzia is the Kimmeridgian, from 154.8 to 152.21 million years ago.
